STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits well up the walls of a white bowl with a curved inner wall visible on the upper side and a shadow inside. The surface is near the rim, so this is a shallow-to-medium bowl, best classed as a salad/serving bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a salad bowl is typically 20-25 cm.
b) Reference: broccoli florets are about 4 cm. Across the bowl I count roughly 5-6 florets laid edge to edge, so width ≈ 5.5 × 4 = 22 cm. Chicken pieces are roughly 2-2.5 cm cubes, and the bowl spans about 10 of them, which gives about 22-25 cm.
Both cues agree on about 23 cm. Final width = 23 cm.

STEP 3 - Items, using a shallow-bowl capacity of 0.2 × width³ / 1000 = 0.2 × 12167 / 1000 ≈ 2.43 L.
Fill: the food sits about 0.8 of the way to the rim, so fill ≈ 0.8, and food volume = 2.43 × 0.8 × 0.8 ≈ 1.56 L = 1560 ml.

Split among items by visible share (estimates):
- Mixed raw leafy greens (spinach/mixed greens): about 45% of volume, ~700 ml × 0.15 g/ml ≈ 105 g.
- Grilled chicken breast cubes: about 25%, ~390 ml × 1.0 g/ml ≈ 390 g. This looks heavy for the visible cube count, so I'll use about 200 g to be realistic (the cubes are fairly sparse and mostly single-layer, which I think is closer to the true amount).
- Broccoli florets (cooked/steamed-looking): about 15%, ~235 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 140 g.
- Avocado slices: about 15%, ~235 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 110 g (avocado is dense, so I use 0.6 as a chopped-fruit density).

Dressing: none is clearly visible beyond a light sheen, so I add a small amount of oil, about 5 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the greens form the base under the toppings, and this is already counted. No separate rice or grain layer is visible.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Mixed greens: ~20 kcal
- Grilled chicken breast: ~165 kcal
- Broccoli, cooked: ~35 kcal
- Avocado: ~160 kcal
- Oil dressing: ~880 kcal

Totals: greens 105 g ≈ 21 kcal; chicken 200 g ≈ 330 kcal; broccoli 140 g ≈ 49 kcal; avocado 110 g ≈ 176 kcal; oil 5 g ≈ 44 kcal. Total ≈ 620 kcal, about 600 g of food.
